title: Matrices
summary: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers. One with m rows and n columns has order m × n; its element in row i and column j is aᵢⱼ. Example: aᵢⱼ = (i − j)/(i + j) gives a₂₃ = −1/5 and a₁₂ = −1/3.

Types: row, column, square, zero, diagonal, scalar (diagonal with equal entries), identity I (scalar with 1s), upper and lower triangular. Every identity matrix is a scalar matrix, but not every scalar matrix is an identity matrix.
Two matrices are equal when they have the same order and equal corresponding elements; equate them entry by entry.
Addition and subtraction need matrices of the same order. Scalar multiplication multiplies every element.
Product AB exists only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B; an m × n times an n × p matrix gives m × p. In general AB ≠ BA, and AB = O does not force A = O or B = O.
A' is obtained by turning rows into columns. (A')' = A, (A + B)' = A' + B', (kA)' = kA' and (AB)' = B'A'.
A is symmetric if A' = A and skew-symmetric if A' = −A; every diagonal element of a skew-symmetric matrix is 0.
If A² = A then (I + A)² − 3A = I + 2A + A² − 3A = I. For A = [[cos α, −sin α], [sin α, cos α]], A + A' = 2 cos α · I, so A + A' = I gives cos α = ½, i.e. α = π/3.

mcq.work: Equal matrices have equal corresponding entries: y = 4, z = 3, x = 1.

objective4: A and B are 2 × 2 matrices with aᵢⱼ = i + j and bᵢⱼ = i − j. Find (i) A + 2B, (ii) AB, (iii) A', (iv) B⁻¹.

True or False: (a) Two matrices are comparable if they have the same number of rows and columns. (b) If A is skew-symmetric, all its diagonal elements are zero. (c) (AB)' = A'B'. (d) If A = [[2, −1, 5], [3, 8, 7]], then A' = [[2, 3], [−1, 8], [5, 7]].

(a) True.
(b) True — aᵢᵢ = −aᵢᵢ ⇒ aᵢᵢ = 0.
(c) False — (AB)' = B'A'.
(d) True — rows become columns.
vsa: For any 3 × 3 matrix A, prove that (A')' = A.

Let A = [aᵢⱼ]. Then A' = [bᵢⱼ] with bᵢⱼ = aⱼᵢ, and (A')' = [cᵢⱼ] with cᵢⱼ = bⱼᵢ = aᵢⱼ.
So (A')' and A have the same order and equal elements: (A')' = A.
For what values of x and y are [[2x + 1, 3y], [0, y² − 5y]] and [[x + 3, y² + 2], [0, −6]] equal?

2x + 1 = x + 3 ⇒ x = 2.
3y = y² + 2 ⇒ y² − 3y + 2 = 0 ⇒ y = 1 or 2.
y² − 5y = −6 ⇒ y² − 5y + 6 = 0 ⇒ y = 2 or 3.
Common value: y = 2. So x = 2, y = 2.
